Container.Name: isputnik
Container.Overview:
Private self-hosted family media library, now in Beta (4.0.0 and later). Audiobooks with a built-in player, ebooks with an in-browser reader, and a photo and video gallery with face recognition (the isputnik-faces container beside it, nothing leaves your server), albums, slideshows rendered to MP4, and a Photo Inbox for scans and photos from relatives. The family writes its own stories and recipes around what the house holds, and keeps a family tree linked to the people found in the photos. Multiple accounts with per-person progress and permissions, sharing and guest links, passkeys and two-factor sign-in, an installable PWA with offline listening, and an English or Russian interface.
Beta means your data is looked after: the database migrates itself forward on every upgrade, a copy of it is saved before each new version starts, and backups can be scheduled from the Control panel. Features are still moving. On first run, open the web UI on your home network to create the administrator account.
Container.Changes:
### 2026.11.11 — 4.84.0 How fast is the TV's connection? - **Test the connection speed from the TV app.** iSputnik TV 0.13.0 can measure how fast it downloads from your server and say what that is enough for, such as *42 Mbit/s: enough for 1080p*. The server sends it a few seconds of data to time. Only signed-in devices can ask, and only a few times a minute.
### 2026.11.11 — 4.83.1 Video progress, easier to see - **Clearer watch progress.** Movie and episode cards now have thicker, rounded progress bars set slightly inside the artwork, with an opaque track and outline. Season counts, resume actions and the home banner use the same treatment. - **Progress and watched checks follow your theme.** Both use the current theme's accent color. Contrasting tracks and outlined check badges keep them visible over artwork in every theme, including Minimalist.
### 2026.11.10 — 4.83.0 Video pages, tidied - **A poster's menu is beside its name.** The ⋮ now sits under the poster, next to the title, on every film and show: always there, never over the picture, and the same with a finger as with a mouse. Before, it appeared over the art only when you pointed at it. The menu also has **Add to My list** and, for a film, **Download**. - **Marks in the corner.** The watched check and a show's "8 unwatched" are in the picture's top-right corner; a film left part-way has a gold bar along its foot. - **One row of buttons on a film's or show's page.** Play, My list, Download for a film, and a ⋮ with the rest: Mark as watched or unwatched, Reset progress, Add to collection and, for admins, Edit. Before, they ran to two rows. - **The season row says where you are.** The season tabs now share one row with "5 of 10 watched", a bar, and the season's ⋮, which marks the whole season and holds **Download season**. - **Episodes.** Each episode's ⋮ is beside its name: Play episode, Mark as watched, Download episode. Its line says how long it runs, and *On this device* once it is downloaded. - Continue watching says how long is left in minutes: *47 min left*.
### 2026.11.10 — 4.82.0 Downloads you don't wait for - **Two ways to download a film or episode.** **Optimized for this device** is a smaller picture: 480p is suggested on a phone (about 0.7 GB for a two-hour film) and 720p on a tablet or computer (about 1.4 GB), and you can pick another. **Full copy** is the file as it is, and starts at once. - **The server prepares an optimized copy, and you don't have to wait for it.** The dialog says about how long it takes. Close iSputnik and come back later: the copy is waiting in Downloads and comes down by itself as soon as the app is open on that device, at the full speed of the connection. Before, the film was converted while the phone waited, which was slow, loaded the server throughout and needed the app open from start to finish. - **Email me when it is ready**, a tick box in the dialog where email is set up and your account has an address. One email per request, so a whole season sends one. - **A prepared copy is kept on the server**, so the next person who wants that film gets it at once. Control panel → Settings → Video → **Copies for download** sets how much room they may take together (20 GB to start with), shows what they take, and removes them all. Copies are made one at a time, on the GPU when the video container has one, and wait while anyone is watching. - A prepared copy is one ordinary MP4, so it plays on any iPhone or iPad; a converted download no longer needs iOS 17.1. - This needs the video container 0.33 or newer; update it with this release. With an older one, an optimized download is still converted while the app waits.
### 2026.11.10 — 4.81.0 What you have watched - **Every video poster says where you are in it.** A bar along the foot of a film you left part-way, a check in the corner of one you finished, and "8 unwatched" on a show you have started; on a show's page each season says 6/10 watched. A title you never started says nothing. Before, a grid of posters could not tell you what was new, started or done. - **Mark it by hand.** A film seen at the cinema, four seasons watched somewhere else, a series to watch again: **Mark as watched** and **Mark as unwatched** are on a film's page, on a show's page for all of it, beside each season's count, and in the **⋮** menu of every episode and every poster. **Reset progress** forgets the place you stopped in a film. The menu offers only what applies. A whole show or season is asked about first. - **Play and Continue watching follow at once.** Mark seasons 1 to 3 watched and season 4's first episode is next; a new episode of a show you had finished brings its count back. - **Filter → Watched** narrows the video page to Unwatched, In progress or Watched, any of them together. - The marks are yours alone: each account, and each viewing profile, has its own. Bars, counts, the filter and marking a whole show or season need the video container 0.32 or newer; with an older one a single film, episode or part can still be marked on its page. The TV app does not show them yet.

Config.Name: Web UI Port
Config.Description: Port used to access the iSputnik web interface.

Config.Name: Config & Data
Config.Description: Stores database, metadata, thumbnails, backups, settings, and application data. Backups appear here under backups/.

Config.Name: Media Storage
Config.Description: Media storage path. Must be Read/Write — uploading photos/videos and filing them into dated folders writes here (scanning alone only needs read). Additional storage locations can be added later by editing the container or from within iSputnik.

Config.Name: PUID
Config.Description: User ID the app runs as. The server runs unprivileged (not root); on first start it takes ownership of the Config & Data path as this user. 99 (nobody) matches the default owner of an Unraid appdata share — leave it unless your share is owned by a different user.

Config.Name: PGID
Config.Description: Group ID the app runs as. 100 (users) matches the default group of an Unraid appdata share — leave it unless your share uses a different group.

Config.Name: App URL
Config.Description: The address the app is reached at (for example https://isputnik.example.com). Set this when you put a reverse proxy or tunnel in front: it fixes the browser origin the app accepts, and an https address is also what turns on HTTPS-only enforcement (HSTS). Leave blank for plain LAN access.

Config.Name: HSTS
Config.Description: Leave blank. When App URL starts with https:// the app tells browsers to stay on HTTPS for a year. Set to false to suppress that — for example when your reverse proxy already sends its own Strict-Transport-Security header. Nothing is sent for a plain-http App URL either way.

Config.Name: Cookie Secure
Config.Description: Leave on auto: secure cookies then follow App URL — on when it starts with https://, off for a plain http home install. Set true or false only to override that. Secure cookies are never sent over plain http, so forcing true on an http install drops the sign-in cookie and you cannot log in. (auto needs version 1.13.3 or newer.)

Config.Name: Session Length (days)
Config.Description: Number of days a login session remains valid.

Config.Name: Linked Device Session Length (days)
Config.Description: Number of days a TV, wall display or other screen signed in with Link a device stays signed in. Each one is listed under Profile, Devices and can be revoked there.

Config.Name: Invite Validity (days)
Config.Description: Number of days invitation links remain valid.

Config.Name: Trusted Proxy Addresses
Config.Description: The reverse proxy's own IP or CIDR range, comma-separated for several (e.g. 172.18.0.0/16 for a Docker network). Preferred over Trusted Proxy Hops: forwarded headers are only believed when they come from these addresses. Leave blank for direct LAN access. Needed for correct per-IP rate limiting, auto-block, and trusted networks.

Config.Name: Trusted Proxy Hops
Config.Description: Alternative to Trusted Proxy Addresses when the proxy's IP isn't fixed: the number of reverse proxies in front of the app (usually 1 behind a reverse proxy or Cloudflare Tunnel). Leave blank for direct LAN access or when Trusted Proxy Addresses is set (addresses win if both are). Set it to match your proxy count, no higher, and don't expose the app's port directly.
